findings: The full DAgger article states the one-step cost-to-go difference premise and its conversion from a surrogate that upper-bounds action disagreement. This is necessary to convert online surrogate loss into task cost; low supervised loss alone is insufficient.

The infinite-sample guarantee uses bounded strongly convex losses/no-regret and expert labeling on interaction policies; its exponentially decaying beta schedule ensures the averaged expert-use term vanishes. The plan now states Theorem 3.2’s epsilon_N and uT cost term.
Theorem 3.3 is a separate finite-sample statement: N=O(T^2 log(1/delta)), m=O(1), Azuma, and an induced-policy surrogate-loss deviation O(1/T). It is not the same as the task-cost guarantee.

findings: Howard et al. Theorem 4 requires adapted observations in [a,b] and predictable forecasts in [a,b]. Its variance clock is observed V_t=sum_i(X_i-hatX_i)^2, not predictable conditional variance; its estimand mu_t is the average conditional mean and no common conditional mean is needed.

For a valid one-sided sub-exponential uniform boundary crossing alpha at scale b-a, the source’s two-sided all-times statement is P(for all t, |barX_t-mu_t|<u(V_t)/t)>=1-2alpha. Set alpha=delta/2 for nominal 1-delta.

Appendix A.8 constructs the scalar exponential supermartingale using the Fan inequality for residuals bounded below by -1. The source proof and theorem are inspected; the boundary may be supplied by upstream mixture/stitching only under product-measurability hypotheses.
Matrix results are excluded because the cited matrix supermartingale facts are not in this source.
